  "question": "What has been proposed to reduce the risk of agents failing to cooperate merely because their source code differs in harmless ways, and by what mechanism?",
  "reference_answer": "FairBot replaces exact source-code matching with proof-based conditional cooperation. It searches for a proof in PA that its opponent will cooperate with it, cooperating if that proof is found and defecting otherwise. When FairBot faces itself, its cooperation condition becomes a self-referential statement equating cooperation with the provability of cooperation. The document evaluates this statement's fixed point as true, yielding cooperation. Because this result does not depend on FairBot's particular implementation, harmless source-code differences need not prevent cooperation, unlike with CliqueBot's exact-code test.",
